data.narrative:
Mojo Vision, founded by Drew Perkins and Michael Wiemer, is a Series B chip design company seeking valuation in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. The analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Positron AI, Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, and Etched at Series A through Series C stages.

Two valuation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis anchors to the company's $345M total raised and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement, implying $656M. Peer-median methodology assesses four same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables—Rebellions ($2.3B, Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series A), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—yielding a median valuation of $1.5B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (20.4x median across the three public tickers) cannot be applied absent target revenue disclosure. The peer range spans $529M to $2.3B.

Triangulating the two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $557M to $1.7B, with a median of $1.1B. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory and competitive positioning relative to the peer set's heterogeneous stages and valuations. The wide peer range ($529M–$2.3B) reflects stage and market timing variance rather than fundamental clarity on Mojo Vision's specific traction.
